title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 61 (Power of Limited Company to Alter Its Share Capital)

content.overview: Section 61 allows a limited company having a share capital, if so authorised by its articles, to alter its memorandum to increase authorised capital; consolidate and divide shares; convert fully paid shares into stock and reconvert; sub-divide shares; or cancel unissued shares. Certain alterations (e.g. consolidation or division that results in a change in voting percentage of shareholders) require Tribunal approval. Cancellation of unissued shares does not amount to a reduction of share capital under the Act.
content.glance: Articles-authorised alteration of capital: increase; consolidate/divide; convert to/from stock; sub-divide; cancel unissued; Tribunal approval where voting percentage changes; cancel ≠ reduction.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 61 (Power of limited company to alter its share capital). A limited company having share capital may, if authorised by its articles, alter its memorandum in general meeting to: (i) increase authorised share capital; (ii) consolidate and divide shares into shares of a larger amount; (iii) convert fully paid shares into stock and reconvert stock into fully paid shares of any denomination; (iv) sub-divide shares into shares of a smaller amount; or (v) cancel shares not taken or agreed to be taken and reduce the share capital by the amount cancelled. Where consolidation or division results in a change in voting percentage of shareholders, Tribunal approval is required. Cancellation of unissued shares under section 61 does not itself amount to reduction of share capital. A notice under section 64 may be required for specified alterations; check the separate filing trigger and deadline.

sections.heading: Authority and general meeting
sections.body: A limited company having share capital may exercise section 61 only if authorised by its articles and by altering its memorandum in general meeting.

sections.heading: Permitted alterations
sections.body: The listed alterations are: increase authorised share capital; consolidate and divide shares into larger-denomination shares; convert fully paid shares into stock and reconvert; sub-divide shares into smaller-denomination shares; or cancel shares not taken or agreed to be taken and reduce capital by the amount cancelled.

sections.heading: Tribunal approval
sections.body: Consolidation or division that results in a change in voting percentage of shareholders requires Tribunal approval.

sections.heading: Cancellation is not reduction
sections.body: Cancellation of shares not taken or agreed to be taken under section 61 does not itself amount to reduction of share capital under the Act.

sections.heading: Separate filing duty
sections.body: For events specified in section 64, the company must separately file the prescribed notice with the Registrar within 30 days. Check whether the particular alteration falls within section 64(1).

provisions.title: Power of limited company to alter its share capital

examples.title: Increase of authorised capital
examples.body: Articles authorise. The company in general meeting increases authorised capital. Section 61 is applied; no Tribunal approval needed for a pure increase.

examples.title: Consolidation affecting voting
examples.body: Consolidation of shares would change voting percentages of shareholders. Tribunal approval is required under s. 61.

hypotheticals.question: Does cancelling unissued shares under s. 61 require the reduction procedure?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 61 expressly provides that such cancellation does not amount to a reduction of share capital under the Act.

distinctions.title: Alteration of capital and reduction of capital
distinctions.left: Section 61 covers specified structural alterations, including cancellation of shares not taken or agreed to be taken.
distinctions.right: Section 66 covers capital reduction by special resolution and NCLT confirmation.

misconceptions.trap: Any capital change under s. 61 needs Tribunal approval.
misconceptions.correction: Tribunal approval is required only where consolidation or division results in a change in voting percentage of shareholders.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Which capital alterations may a limited company make under section 61?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Increase authorised capital; consolidate/divide; convert fully paid shares into stock and reconvert; sub-divide; or cancel shares not taken or agreed to be taken.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When does section 61 require Tribunal approval?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Where consolidation or division results in a change in voting percentage of shareholders.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Does cancellation of unissued shares under section 61 count as reduction?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. Section 61 expressly distinguishes this cancellation from a reduction of share capital.
